risk_if_not_implemented: Without Sensitive / Regulated Data Sharing Decisions, sensitive and/or regulated data may be disclosed, altered or lost through inadequate classification, handling or protection. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Lack of a security-minded workforce (R-SA-2), Loss of Confidentiality (R-IP-2), and most likely increases susceptibility to Human Error (MT-9).

compensating_control_1.name: Third-Party Contract Requirements
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to require contractual requirements for applicable security, compliance and resilience requirements with third-parties, reflecting the organization's needs to protect its Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD).
compensating_control_1.justification: Third-Party Contract Requirements (TPM-14) provides third-party oversight that compensates for the absence of Information Sharing (DCH-08.1) by extending security obligations contractually and monitoring third-party risk in lieu of direct control. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Encrypting Data In Transit
compensating_control_2.description: Cryptographic mechanisms exist to prevent the unauthorized disclosure of data in transit.
compensating_control_2.justification: Encrypting Data In Transit (CRY-05) provides cryptographic protection that compensates for the absence of Information Sharing (DCH-08.1) by ensuring data confidentiality and integrity through alternative technical means. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
